title: security_next.py --claim takes only the top alert, while each alert file asks a run to fix and claim its whole same-file batch
problem: alerts/<n>.md (security_alerts.py) says: fix every queued alert in the same file (and the same rule in sibling files) in one PR, claiming each one's branch too. security_next.py --claim claimed one alert, so runs claimed the rest by hand with the alert file's `git checkout -b ... origin/main && git push`. That push is not race-safe: a second run pushing the same origin/main sha gets 'Everything up-to-date', exit 0, and both think they won (the bug PR #18851 fixed inside claim()).
evidence: promptctl measure, 'Doc friction by file', platform/ci/security_next.py: 9 reports, 5 in the 3 days to 2026-11-27; 2026-11-27T06:58: '--claim takes only the top alert, but alerts/<n>.md asks a run to batch every queued alert in the same file and rule and claim each; there is no flag to claim a list'
origin/security-alerts:alerts/1489.md on 2026-11-27: step 1 names the hand push; step 2 names the batch
change: --claim also claims the top alert's batch (batch_of: same file, or same rule in the same directory) with the race-safe claim(), naming each number won or lost; --no-batch takes one. The alert files' step 1 now names security_next.py --claim instead of the hand push.
metric: security_next.py friction reports about claiming a batch or a list, 14 days after merge
baseline: 5 reports in 3 days to 2026-11-27 (1 naming the batch directly)
